articleTitle: A new technique for measuring the microwave properties of high temperature superconducting rods
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on What's New in Microwave Measurements
abstract: This paper presents a new technique capable of investigating anisotropy in high temperature superconducting rods using two closely-spaced modes in a co-axial copper cavity at frequencies around 20 GHz. The two-mode method of anisotropy evaluation is shown to be simple and reliable. So far, R/sub sa//R/sub sc/ ratios as low as 0.5 have been achieved by zone annealing. Frequency dependence can also be measured by sweeping additional modes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Precision radar measurements using a novel compact test range
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on What's New in Microwave Measurements
abstract: A compact radar test range is reported. The range is capable of coupling a fully operational W-band, dual-axis, dual polarised seeker system to a transponder which generates simulated target and clutter returns while allowing full seeker antenna movement. The range is considerably more compact, less complex and less expensive than currently used techniques. Its operation relies on the close coupling of the seeker antenna to a transponder antenna with a similar sized aperture. Both antennas face into a single 4 foot diameter ellipsoidal reflector. With one antenna at each of the reflectors foci, whichever direction the radar beam is directed it will always be incident on the transponder antenna. The beam of the transponder antenna is directed by a flat scanning plate in order to obtain constant coupling loss. Less than +or-0.5 dB variation in coupling loss is achieved over scanning angles of at least +or-30 degrees in both the azimuth and elevation axes, thus allowing accurate sensitivity measurements to be made. Minimum distortion occurs to the seeker antenna radiation patterns which means that the monopulse discriminator performance is maintained and the ground detection and target tracking performance can be evaluated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on What's New in Microwave Measurements
abstract: This paper describes some research work that will be carried out with the support of the SERC over the next three years. The work is part of a larger grant which involves the production of MMICs at 140 GHz. The author's contribution to this research is to provide the measurement facility for on-wafer probing at these frequencies. Two problems arise at the out-set, which are the lack of commercial network analysers and the high attenuation of metallic waveguides at 140 GHz. The paper describes an alternative to a network analyser which the author has already used for measurements in the range 70-110 GHz (Collier and D'Souza, 1991). Also the paper discusses a technique which avoids the problems of metallic waveguide. Finally some comments are made about probes for these frequencies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on What's New in Microwave Measurements
abstract: This contribution describes methods for determining the surface impedance of powders, single crystals and thin films of high-Tc superconductors, and the properties of circuits containing active devices. These methods are used for investigation of superconductor physics and for development of production processes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Complex microwave noise parameter measurement using a coaxial radiometer
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on What's New in Microwave Measurements
abstract: A technique has been described for the measurement of the complex noise parameters of an active device using a computer controlled coaxial radiometer designed for noise source calibration. The uncertainties on the measured parameters are fully traceable to National Standards. The current values yield an uncertainty of +or-0.2 dB in noise figure at the 95% confidence level. This is limited largely by the uncertainty on the primary noise standard to which all the noise source calibrations are traceable. This primary standard will be replaced in the near future and a lower uncertainty level is predicted. The system used is limited to the frequency band 10 MHz to 18 GHz, but the technique can in principle be applied to any total power radiometer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The accurate measurement of attenuation and phase
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on What's New in Microwave Measurements
abstract: This paper describes techniques which allow the traceable measurement, at low uncertainty values, of attenuation levels up to at least 140 dB at frequencies from 0.5 MHz to 100 MHz. In addition the techniques allow the phase changes through the attenuator to be measured accurately at the high attenuation levels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on What's New in Microwave Measurements
abstract: The increasing demand for wide band calibrations of coaxial power sensors has prompted NPL to undertake the development of a 3.5 mm coaxial power standard. The system currently under development uses a twin load dry cell coaxial calorimeter where the objective is to provide calibration over the range 0.1 mW to 10 mW with an uncertainty better than 0.25% from DC to 33 GHz. In the design of the 3.5 mm coaxial calorimeter a number of difficulties have arisen due to the physical dimensions of the lines and the manufacturing tolerances involved. This paper discusses some of these problems and provides a report on the current status of the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Traceable reflection coefficient measurements in coaxial line at MF and HF
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on What's New in Microwave Measurements
abstract: This paper describes a measurement capability developed at NPL Malvern to provide traceability for complex voltage reflection coefficients at MF and HF (300 kHz to 30 MHz). A vector indicating automatic network analyser (ANA) is used as a reflectometer and is calibrated in terms of a calculable open-circuit, a short-circuit and a characterised load. The load is characterised using a frequency-invariant equivalent-circuit model derived from measurement data at higher frequencies. The equivalent-circuit details are given, along with results achieved using this capability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
